prompt.context: A travel agency has set up a centralized call center where all incoming phone calls from all branches are diverted to. Shortly after setting up the call center, the travel agency is virtually unreachable because of the large amount of phone calls received.
prompt.question: What could cause the overload of the call center?

clarifying_info.q: Is the overload caused by technical problems or peaks in demand?
clarifying_info.a: Assume the overload is not caused by technical problems or peaks in demand; it is solely caused by the fact that the amount of required agents does not match the number of agents in the center.

clarifying_info.q: How many agents are required in week 20?
clarifying_info.a: Use the exhibit showing cumulative diverted customers. From it, approximately 140,000 customers are diverted by week 20. Other data: average call time = 240 seconds, average wrap-up time = 60 seconds, working hours per agent = 40 hours/week, gross/net ratio ~80%, working time duration ~50%. Assume average calls per customer = 2 per year, seasonal pattern = 0%.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average number of calls per customer?
clarifying_info.a: Assume 2 calls per customer per year.

clarifying_info.q: What is the seasonal pattern for week 20?
What are the call and wrap-up times?
clarifying_info.a: Average call time is 240 seconds; average wrap-up time is 60 seconds.

clarifying_info.q: How many hours does an agent work per week?
What is the gross/net working hours ratio?
clarifying_info.a: Approximately 80% (about 1.5 hours lost per day to breaks: (8-1.5)/8 ≈ 81%).

clarifying_info.q: What is the working time duration (percentage of time on calls)?

exhibits.title: Cumulative Number of Customers Diverted to the Centralized Call Center
exhibits.shows: A line chart with weeks (0–60) on the x-axis and cumulative number of customers (0–1,200,000) on the y-axis, showing growth in diverted customers since the call center was set up at week 0.

framework: Required number of agents = Call Volume × Average Settlement Time / Capacity per Agent
Call Volume drivers: (1) Number of diverted customers, (2) Average number of calls per customer, (3) Seasonal pattern
Average Settlement Time = Call time (seconds) + Wrap-up time (seconds)
Capacity per Agent = Working hours per agent × Gross/Net ratio × Working time duration

questions.prompt: What could cause the overload of the call center?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure causes into supply, technical, and demand categories. Look for MECE structure with specific sub-causes under each bucket.

questions.prompt: How would you calculate the required number of agents needed to fix the problem?
questions.guidance: Candidate must build a driver tree: Required agents = (Call volume × Average settlement time) / Capacity per agent. Then decompose each: Call volume = (diverted customers / 52 weeks) × calls per customer × seasonal factor; Settlement time = call time + wrap-up time; Capacity = working hours × gross/net ratio × working time duration. Key insight: agents are not 100% productive — only ~40% of their time is spent on actual calls.

questions.prompt: How many agents are required in week 20?
questions.guidance: Read ~140,000 from the exhibit. Calculate weekly call volume, apply settlement time, and divide by agent capacity. Should arrive at ~28–29 agents.

math.setup: Required agents = (Calls per week × Settlement time per call) / Capacity per agent per week
steps: Settlement time per call = 240 sec + 60 sec = 300 sec = 5 min = 1/12 hour
Capacity per agent per week = 40 h × 80% × 50% = 16 hours/week
math.answer: Approximately 28–29 agents are required in week 20.

questions.prompt: There are no additional trained call center agents available. What other ways can you think of to help the travel agency with its telephone problem?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the driver tree structure from the previous question. There are three levers: (1) reduce call volume, (2) reduce average settlement time, (3) increase capacity per agent. Strong candidates will generate specific actionable solutions under each lever.

brainstorming.prompt: What ways can you think of to help the travel agency reduce overload without hiring new agents?

categories.name: Reduce Call Volume
ideas: Stop diverting calls from branches to call center and revert some calls back to branches
Insert a computer-based interactive voice response (IVR) menu that answers the most frequently asked questions automatically

categories.name: Reduce Average Settlement Time
ideas: Monitor wrap-up times to identify and streamline the most common wrap-up actions
Introduce a computer application that assists agents with standard wrap-up actions (e.g., automatically sending brochures) to cut wrap-up time

categories.name: Increase Capacity per Agent
ideas: Align agent scheduling with actual demand patterns — mobilize more agents during peaks and fewer during lows
Encourage part-time arrangements so peak periods can be covered with flexible staffing
Improve the gross/net working ratio by reviewing break schedules

recommendation: The call center overload is driven by a mismatch between required and actual agents; in week 20 approximately 28–29 agents are needed

In the short term, reduce call volume via IVR/FAQ deflection and revert lower-priority calls back to branches; in the medium term, re-align agent scheduling to demand patterns and streamline wrap-up processes
risks: Customer satisfaction may decline further if call deflection (IVR) is poorly designed
Branch staff may be overwhelmed if calls are diverted back without adequate preparation
Seasonal demand spikes could still cause overloads if only structural fixes are made
next_steps: Audit which call types can be deflected via IVR or answered via self-service
Implement demand-aligned scheduling and track working time duration KPI
Monitor cumulative diverted customers weekly to anticipate when additional agents will be required
